title: Micro-profiling for wordpiece-level latency and cache-economics
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Surface per-wordpiece emission timings and the incremental cost/latency impact of KV cache hits/misses across the serving runtime, then roll those signals into the metrics/log pipeline and dashboarding so product and SRE teams can attribute token-level cost and regressions to specific model versions, kernel choices, or cache policies.

Background: Current observability gives coarse per-request latency and aggregated token counts. We lack visibility into where time is spent inside the emission pipeline (decode loop, kernel launch, KV cache lookup/restore, prefix reuse) and how cache hit patterns change unit economics. This forces manual sampling and ad-hoc tracing when debugging latency regressions or comparing quantization/kernel variants.

Approach:
- Tracing hooks: add lightweight micro-spans at wordpiece boundaries: pre-decode, post-decode, kv-lookup-start, kv-lookup-end, kernel-invoke-start, kernel-invoke-end, emit-serialize. Each span is tagged with model_id, model_version, deployment_type (hosted/dedicated/private), route, request_id, and a cache_tag (hit|miss|partial). Spans are optional and controlled via sampling flags and a per-route feature flag to avoid high cardinality in hot paths.
- KV cache tagging: instrument the cache layer to emit an event when a prefix hit occurs and include delta bytes recovered, cache_latency_us, and a cache_score tag. Provide a small API surface so runtime can annotate whether retrieved KV entries were reused or trimmed.
- Metrics/log pipeline: create a new high-cardinality trace->metric extractor job in the existing telemetry pipeline that converts sampled micro-spans into two outputs: 1) per-wordpiece histograms (latency_us) aggregated by model_version, route, and cache_tag, and 2) per-request aggregated deltas (total_token_latency_us, cache_saved_us, kernel_time_us). Use off-peak rollups (1m/5m) to keep storage sane.
- Schema & naming: follow observable naming conventions: rw.token.latency.wordpiece_us, rw.token.count.reused, rw.cache.latency_us, rw.token.cost.delta_cents. Tag keys: model, version, deployment, route, cache_tag, kernel_variant.
- Dashboards & alerts: new dashboard panels for wordpiece latency P50/P95/P99 by model_version and cache_tag, a heatmap of per-position latency growth for long contexts, and a chart comparing per-token cost delta across kernel/quantization variants. Add an alert when P95 wordpiece latency increases >20% for a model_version over a 1h window.
- Rollout: implement behind a runtime flag initially sampled at 1% of requests for hosted API and 0.1% for Dedicated. After validation (no perf regression and manageable telemetry volume), ramp to 10% then enable coarse rollups for 100% (no trace payloads for all).
- Privacy: spans must avoid payload/text capture. Only metadata and timing are recorded. No user prompt content, keys, or PII allowed in traces.
- Backwards compatibility: ensure telemetry fields are additive and dashboards default to models with existing time series. Provide data migration queries to backfill aggregated metrics for historical comparison where possible.
- Validation: run A/B experiments comparing cost estimates from new metrics to billing estimates on a sample of customers to validate accuracy within 5%.

Operational concerns: telemetry volume, cardinality explosion (mitigated by sampling and tag pruning), and runtime overhead (target <0.5% median latency increase when sampling enabled).

Deliverables: instrumentation PRs (runtime + cache layer), telemetry extractor job, Prometheus/ClickHouse metric mapping, Grafana dashboard panels, alert rules, rollout runbook, and post-rollout cost validation report.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes micro-span hooks at wordpiece boundaries with stable tag schema and runtime flag control
KV cache emits cache_tag and delta metrics and can annotate reuse vs partial hits
Telemetry extractor converts sampled spans into per-wordpiece histograms and per-request deltas; rollups at 1m/5m exist
Grafana dashboard with P50/P95/P99 by model_version and cache_tag is available and documented
Alerting rule firing for >20% P95 wordpiece latency regression over 1h is implemented
End-to-end benchmark shows sampling overhead <0.5% median latency and telemetry volume within budget at 10% sampling
Privacy checklist signed: no prompt text or PII in traces
Post-rollout cost validation shows per-token cost delta estimates correlate with billing within 5% on sampled workloads
